post_title: dart seam allowance - issue with union options
post_details: Hello, I've seen several posts on this topic dating back up to 4 years. I'm using the latest version of clo on a mac and finding that on a pattern with darts drafted with the internal polygon tool, the seam allowance option for darts is inconsistently available. all darts in this pattern were drafted the same. The option for the dart union was at first not available at all after applying seam allowance. Upon switching tools, it was available for one dart. Then after repeating that exercise it was available again for the second. I cannot get it to come up for the third dart, despite clicking on the dart point. is this a glitch or am I missing something?

comments.comment_body: Hi 27642453136665 For Darts on pattern edges you must use the Add Dart Function. By Selecting a Single Segment Point &gt R-Click with the Edit pattern Tool &gt Select Add Dart. Then once you have applied Seam Allowance Use the Seam Allowance Tool to click the Dart point (only that 1 point) &gt You will see the options in the Property Editor under the Intersection dropdown. Please note that some dart shapes that exceed certain angles or if the dart legs are not even you will not be acle to change the dart seam allowance to a cap. But this is a feature request which is being worked on

post_title: grading with a spec - help please
post_details: Hello! New to clo3d and hoping for some help here I have a size range (comprehensive body measurements) set for sizes from 0 18. I want to grade my patterns to fit each size without needing to manually adjust specific pattern points, but by grading to fit the specified body measurements. What is the best method to do this? Is there a way I can enter this spec into clo so I can auto grade using my unique body size spec? Or perhaps I need to create custom size avatars across all sizes and then use the clo auto grade function to grade the patterns to each size? Many thanks! Sarah

comments.comment_body: Hi 27642453136665, It is better to understand the Auto Grading tool as an Auto Fitting tool. It will fit a garment onto the measurements of an avatar, but there is no guarantee you don't have to go in and do further edits to get the accurate desired result. Aside from this as a possibility, there is no automated way of grading in CLO.
Thank you for the insights. Is there a way to create a customized grade rule that I may apply to my patterns rather than manually grading each pattern by point?
Hi 27642453136665, This is not possible yet, but we will add it as a request for developers to consider :)

Thank you kindly for considering this feature. I've just seen other similar requests as well. As you know its not uncommon to have grades set for specific categories of garment types. Say a specific grade one would use for all slim woven tops or another for all t-shirts for example. it would be a huge time saver and an advantage to have a consistent grade rule to simply set within a form, and then be able select it to apply as patterns are developed.

post_title: Seams get pointed probably due to tension
post_details: Sometimes seam line gets pointed due to tension of near seams(I'm not sure exactly what causes this issue). I don't think this issue would occur in a real toile. How to fix it?

comments.comment_body: Hi 903947214646, In CLO, fabrics cannot rip as in real life, they can stretch and the fit has to be determined via Garment Fit Maps. So you are correct this wouldn't happen IRL. The waistband is too tight where it is sitting, and the look can be relaxed and made more true to life by applying hires properties (Skin Offset of avatar down to 0, PD of the pattern pieces down to 5, and Add'l Thickness Collision down to 1). You can also apply elastic to the lower edge of the waistband, set it to 100, so it doesn't stretch out due to being sewn onto a line that is longer. When doing the latter, you can notice that the garment might change its position a bit while moving towards the smallest point of the waist. If all of these options do not fix the look, it might simply be that the waistband is still too tight by sheer measurement. In this case, if you do not wish to widen the pattern pieces involved, you can apply a fabric to the waistband that has high elasticity.

comments.comment_body: Hi 19268783648537 I have also seen your ticket sent through our Contact Us page So I was able to take a look at the image files. Now our tech team will be able to give a better technical answer. But I will do my best below. The first thing I noticed is that the Graphics you are applying are VERY large and while people tend to think larger is better for images that is not true. The image you have shown above (PINK) is so large that CLO needs to compress the image for the 3D preview. You will then notice if you go to the Render window the graphic is much clearer. The pixel size of this image is11161 by 33319 and 134MB(most prints and graphics only need to by 1 or less MB usually). For pixels It is also important to note that with pixels they should be even numbers and divisible by 2. Also note that if you are applying an image as a graphic like you have done you want to make sure you are exporting the PNG with just what you need. Your original image for this one had lots of large yellow and pink boxes (i do not know if these are intended to be seen). But instead export what you need. Or if you are applying as a fabric texture you want it to be a clean JPEG repeat without gaps or edges of the artboard showing which would result in white spaces or areas that look like holes in the fabric So I took the image and resized a smaller portion or the overall image. 3115 x 4096 pixels (not ideal, but quick) and exported the PNG image which was only 17MB (still very large, but manageable) Once applied in CLO, CLO no longer needs to compress since the image is easier to handle so you will see that both the 3D preview and render look nice and clear

I hope you find this helpful. I am also linking a few tutorials I found that talk about image size and pixels you may find useful https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aoDUMcknx9o https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D7Uz8stZnd0 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U4PewSAqa9Y
